title: Hanging Leg Raise
summary: Hang from a bar and curl the hips up toward the chest. Abs 1, obliques 0.5, with grip as a limit.

muscles.why: The rectus abdominis flexes the spine. It only works hard here when the pelvis curls up (posterior tilt); just lifting the legs is mostly hip-flexor work.
The obliques help flex the spine and keep the body from swinging.
You hang by your hands for the whole set (swap tag 'More grip demand').

setup.text: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip, arms straight.
Pull the shoulders slightly down so you are not hanging loose.
Start with bent knees if straight legs are too hard.

form_cues.cue: Curl the pelvis up as the legs rise
form_cues.why: Curling the pelvis is the spinal flexion that trains the abs.

form_cues.cue: Raise legs to at least hip height
form_cues.why: Hip height is the minimum range for the hips to start curling.
A swing turns the rep into momentum.

form_cues.cue: Curling your pelvis up is what works the abs. Just lifting your legs mostly works the hip flexors.
form_cues.why: The pelvis curl is the ab part of the rep; leg lift alone is the hip flexors.
Many lifters find it easier to round the spine on the exhale.

bias_tweaks.change: Bent knees, then straight legs as you get stronger
bias_tweaks.effect: Straight legs lengthen the lever and make the same curl harder.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Only harder if the pelvis still curls; otherwise it just loads the hip flexors.

bias_tweaks.change: Raise the knees toward one shoulder, then the other
bias_tweaks.effect: Adds trunk rotation and side bending, so the obliques work more.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Same total sets; the app still credits obliques at the library rating.
Or switch to a captain's chair (no grip demand).

mistakes.text: Swinging the legs instead of curling the hips.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the bottom and start each rep from a still hang.

mistakes.text: Only lifting the legs without curling the pelvis.
mistakes.fix: Think 'show your belt buckle to your chin'.

mistakes.text: Dropping the legs fast between reps.

misconceptions.myth: Leg raises train the 'lower abs' and crunches the 'upper abs'.
misconceptions.reality: The rectus abdominis is one muscle. Regional differences in growth have not been shown well; pick the movement you can load and progress.
Training a muscle doesn't selectively reduce the fat over it; visible abs mostly depend on body-fat level. The app does not model fat loss.

lower_risk.text: When you add load, the app suggests one bodyweight-only set of 5 first (assisted machines: one set with one step more assistance). Without added load the first working set is its own warm-up.
The app counts your effective load (bodyweight share plus added load) and suggests more weight only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Stop the set when you can no longer curl the pelvis or start to swing.
If hanging is hard on your hands or shoulders, use a captain's chair or ab slings.

alternatives.why: Same knee raise with forearm pads, so grip is not a limit.
Loadable spinal flexion on a cable; easy to progress in small steps.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Needs only a wheel; anti-extension work that trains the abs and obliques (obliques 0.6).

notes: Ab-exercise comparisons for growth are scarce; the choices here are biomechanics or modeled.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
